    Making accessible technology with and for people with disabilities

    Despite progress in tech and society, people with disabilities still face barriers to accessible experiences — including hurdles to complete tasks, navigate the world, or reach their dreams. As creative technologists, we all have an opportunity and a responsibility to ensure what we're building works for everyone.

    Additional accessibility resources

    • Google for Education Accessibility Website

      Google for Education helps students and educators customize their learning tools and create more inclusive learning environments so they can study, teach, and collaborate with confidence. With accessibility features built directly into Chromebooks and the collaborative power of Google Workspace for Education, educators can create tailored learning experiences for every student.

      Explore the Education site

    • Google Accessibility Help and Community

      Find documentation and troubleshooting for using assistive technology with Google products and get support from the Community.

      Explore the Help site

    • Android Accessibility Website

      Built with and for people with disabilities. Android’s accessibility features help you engage with your world, your way. Have conversations, get work done, be entertained, tick off daily tasks, and so much more.

      Explore the Android site

    • Cloud Accessibility Website

      Built with and for people with disabilities, Google Cloud is committed to creating a more accessible enterprise experience. This site serves as a central hub for Google Cloud’s accessibility resources to empower all users — including the global community of 1 billion people with disabilities.

      Explore the Cloud site

    • Natively Adaptive Interfaces (NAI) Website

      The Natively Adaptive Interfaces (NAI) research framework prioritizes user-centered design, embedding accessibility within multimodal AI tools to create interfaces that adapt to a wide range of user abilities and contexts.

      Explore the NAI site

    • Google Accessibility Conformance Reports

      To make it easier for companies, educational institutions, and government agencies to verify alignment with accessibility standards, we provide transparent reports about how our products currently work for people with disabilities. We offer the following English-language Accessibility Conformance Reports (ACR) based on the ITI Voluntary Product Accessibility Template (VPAT®).

      Explore the ACR site

    Prioritizing accessible design to build a more useful world for everyone.


    Google is committed to building more accessible and useful products and services, including by meeting the requirements of the European Accessibility Act (EAA). We continue to monitor the most recent developments in international standards and interpretations of relevant laws. Furthermore, we are engaged in policy conversations and contribute to the development of technical accessibility standards across the industry.


    For many years, Google teams have incorporated accessibility into our products and services. We prioritize continuous education and promote accessibility knowledge across our teams. Our dedicated accessibility teams consult on design, development, and testing to ensure our employees are equipped to create accessible experiences. We also collaborate with the disability community to understand how our products and services can bridge gaps and foster a more accessible world. We are dedicated to ensuring continuous and effective access to our products for all people.
